findings.affected_surface: Python public API / CLI queryformat parsing
findings.old_behavior: The fmt_repl inner function receives the query tag key from the regex match and checks it directly against ALLOWED_QUERY_TAGS (all lowercase). If the key is uppercase (e.g., '%{NAME}'), it does not match any allowed tag and is passed through literally via brackets(). Only lowercase keys like '%{name}' are recognized and substituted with package attribute values.
findings.new_behavior: The fmt_repl inner function calls key.lower() at the start, converting any uppercase tag to lowercase before checking against ALLOWED_QUERY_TAGS. Both '%{NAME}' and '%{name}' are now recognized and substituted with the corresponding package attribute value. The behavior for lowercase tags is unchanged; the return format string now uses the already-lowered key variable instead of calling .lower() again.
findings.compatibility_reason: This patch restores support for uppercased query tags (e.g., '%{NAME}', '%{RELEASE}', '%{REPONAME}') that was unintentionally lost in commit e50488b6 (v4.15.0). Users who specify query tags in uppercase will now see the corresponding package attribute values instead of literal tag text. This is a backward-compatible relaxation of the input contract: existing lowercase-only inputs continue to work identically. The change mirrors rpm's behavior where both uppercase and lowercase query tags are accepted.
findings.why_not_internal_only: rpm2py_format is a module-level public function (no underscore prefix) used by the RepoQueryCommand CLI command. The change is reachable via dnf repoquery --queryformat= with uppercase tag names, which is a CLI surface visible to all DNF users and scripts.
findings.uncertainty: The change is a straightforward input relaxation. The only uncertainty is whether any user-depended-on uppercase tags being passed through literally in v4.15.0+ (between the regression and this fix), which is unlikely given the narrow window and restoration of pre-existing behavior.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that the test case using uppercase tags (%{NAME}, %{RELEASE}, %{REPONAME}) produces the expected output. Confirm that existing lowercase-based queryformat strings are unaffected.
findings.test_recommendation: Run tests.test_repoquery::OutputTest::test_output which exercises uppercase query tags. Also verify that the existing lowercase-based tests still pass. Regression-test that %{name} behavior is unchanged.
